title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 45-46). Grothendieck sets up four kinds of objects in a k-additive category B: chain complexes B_., simplicial objects B_*, cochain complexes B^., and cosimplicial objects B^*. The Dold-Puppe equivalences connect them: ND (normalization) and DP (Dold-Puppe inverse). He also has a k-linear 'universal' category K with four functors alpha_., alpha_*, alpha^., alpha^* into the four kinds of complexes.

First lines. For the distinguished objects C^i of K he identifies the image under alpha_* as alpha_*(C^i) ≃ DP(C^i_.) ≃ Λ^{i+1} L_*. Here L_* is a basic simplicial k-module. So the elementary indecomposable pieces of the universal (co)simplicial object are exterior powers of one fixed simplicial module. Dually, alpha^*(C_i) ≃ DP(C_i^.) ≃ Λ^{i+1} of the dual of L_*. A natural reading, which fits the rank count C(n, i+1), is the décalage-type identification Λ^{i+1}(K(k,1)) ≃ K(k,i+1); the exact choice of L_* is not legible here. A struck-out passage tries to express the adjunction equivalence between these objects and the ND functor, and a struck-out 'Cor. 1' starts a statement about DP on Ab_k.

Main argument.
- Let A be the free k-linear category on a cochain complex: objects C^i (i ≥ 0) and differentials d: C^i → C^{i+1} with d² = 0.
- Let K be its additive hull. K is additive and stable under direct factors (Karoubian), at least when k is such that finitely generated projectives are free (e.g. k principal, k = Z).
- Apply Dold-Puppe inside K to the universal cochain complex C^.. This gives a cosimplicial object C^* = DP(C^.) in K.
- For any k-additive B there is a chain of functors:
  - Hom_{k-lin}(K, B) → Hom_{k-lin}(A, B), by restriction; this is an equivalence because K is the additive hull of A.
  - Hom_{k-lin}(A, B) ≃ B^., via F ↦ F(C^.).
  - DP: B^. → B^*.
- The composite is F ↦ F(C^*). It is fully faithful because DP is fully faithful for any additive B. When B is Karoubian, DP_B is an equivalence, so F ↦ F(C^*) is too.

Prop 5. For B k-additive and Karoubian, F ↦ F(C^*) is an equivalence Hom_{k-lin}(K, B) → B^*. So C^* is the universal cosimplicial object among k-additive Karoubian categories, and K is the free k-linear Karoubian category on a cosimplicial object. Equivalently, Kar(add k[Δ]) ≃ add(free k-linear category on a cochain complex). This is Dold-Kan recast as an equivalence of universal (Karoubi-completed) categories.

The page ends by starting a canonical bifunctorial bijection between functors F: K → B and (co)simplicial objects x of B, continued on p. 47.

Purpose. This builds a uniform 'universal object' framework in which simplicial and cosimplicial objects in additive categories are treated as k-linear functors out of K. That framework is used for the dévissage of ½-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes and multiplicative structures named in the folder title.
errors: The Karoubian property of K (the additive hull of the free category on a cochain complex) is not automatic for arbitrary k. Grothendieck correctly hedges ('du moins si k est ...'). The correct condition is roughly that f.g. projective k-modules are free (k principal/local), not 'parfait'.
Prop 5 needs B Karoubian. Without it the functor is only fully faithful, and Grothendieck says exactly this. No genuine error.

The identification alpha_*(C^i) ≃ Λ^{i+1} L_* depends on the unstated definition of L_*. With an index shift, one should check ranks: Λ^{i+1}(k^n) has rank C(n, i+1) = rank of K(k, i+1)_n. The written indexing could not be verified from the image.

ideas.what: Dold-Kan/Dold-Puppe equivalence between cochain complexes and cosimplicial objects in any k-additive Karoubian category
ideas.modern_name: Dold-Kan correspondence for idempotent-complete additive categories
ideas.where_published: Used implicitly in Illusie's Complexe cotangent (Dold-Puppe); not stated in this form by Grothendieck as far as known

ideas.what: K = free k-linear Karoubian category on a cosimplicial object, equivalent to the additive hull of the free category on a cochain complex; C^* = DP(C^.) is the universal cosimplicial object (Prop 5)
ideas.modern_name: Dold-Kan as an equivalence of Karoubi envelopes, Kar(Z[Δ]) ≃ Kar(Z[free chain complex]); 'categorical equivalences of Dold-Kan type'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; made explicit by Lack-Street ('Combinatorial categorical equivalences of Dold-Kan type', 2015), also Lurie HA 1.2.4

ideas.what: Indecomposable summands of the universal simplicial object identified with exterior powers Λ^{i+1} of a basic simplicial module
ideas.modern_name: Décalage / Λ^n(K(k,1)) ≃ K(k,n); Eilenberg-MacLane simplicial modules as indecomposables of Kar(k[Δ^op])

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates Dold-Kan as a universal property. The k-linear Karoubian category generated by a cochain complex is the free k-linear Karoubian category on a cosimplicial object, with universal object DP(C^.). He also notes the dependence on k (Karoubian only for suitable k). This anticipates the 'Dold-Kan type equivalence of Karoubi envelopes' viewpoint later published by Lack-Street.
missed.quote: C^* apparaît comme objet simplicial universel dans cat. k-additive karoubienne
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical priority: the categorical form of Dold-Kan appears here around 1975-76, some decades before its systematic treatment. The mathematics itself is now standard.

missed.claim: The universal objects are tied to exterior powers of a basic simplicial module (Λ^{i+1} L_*). This links the formal Dold-Kan universality to décalage and Koszul-type structures, presumably for the multiplicative structures named in the folder title.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could interest work on multiplicative Dold-Kan (cosimplicial algebras, the Eilenberg-Zilber/Alexander-Whitney interplay) via universal categories. The page itself gives only the identification.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the Dold-Kan correspondence reformulated as a universal-object/free-Karoubian-category statement. It is elegant and early, but the result is folklore and later explicitly published (Lack-Street, Lurie). The exterior-power identification is classical décalage.
transcription_corrections: 'Appliquant le topos [?] de Dold-Puppe' should read 'Appliquant le théorème de Dold-Puppe'.
'stable par sommes [?] directes' is more likely 'stable par facteurs directs' (i.e. Karoubian), consistent with the following 'si B est karoubienne'.
'du moins si k est parfait [?], p.ex. k = Z' is likely 'si k est principal' (or similar); Z is not 'parfait' in any relevant sense.
'C^* = DP(C^.)' is correct; the struck line reads roughly '(qui est donc défini dans K(k) quel que soit k)'.
Final line: 'x ∈ Ob B^{K}' is likely 'x ∈ Ob B^*' (cosimplicial objects of B).
Struck header line likely: 'L'équ. adj. entre les α(C^i) et l'équivalence ... dans le foncteur ND : K_* → K_. est donnée comme α(Λ^{i+1} L_*)'.
